data.narrative:
Manifold Bio is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Gleb Kuznetsov and Pierce Ogden that has raised $40M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public biotech firms (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-sector peers including Colossal Biosciences, Abridge, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method proved applicable. Using total capital raised of $40M as a proxy for post-money valuation and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $80M. This step-up assumption reflects standard dilution and expected value creation between rounds in early-stage biotech. Peer-median analysis was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum threshold (need ≥3 datapoints; identified only 1 adjacent-stage peer). Public-comp anchoring could not proceed without target revenue disclosure, though the 3-ticker public median P/S of 5.6x establishes a sector reference point.

The triangulated valuation range is $68M to $92M, with a median of $80M. This narrow range reflects reliance on a single method rather than robust cross-validation. Key uncertainties include undisclosed revenue metrics, absence of closely-matched private peers at identical stage and tier, and limited public comparable data. Further valuation refinement would require either revenue visibility or access to transaction data from materially similar Series A biotech financings.
